items.title: The DRC Ebola outbreak passes 10,000 cases: what that milestone means, and where the vaccine trial stands
items.angle: A short, sharp item: the size of this outbreak in context, what the newly launched WHO vaccine trial can and can't do at this scale, and an honest answer on US risk.
items.why_now: The case count reportedly crossed 10,000 days after WHO announced a vaccine trial in DRC, and 'ebola' is rising in general search today.
items.is_it_real: The vaccine trial start is reported by Al Jazeera. The 10,000 figure comes from secondary aggregation and is flagged for verification; confirm it against the latest WHO situation report before writing. Big outlets have staff on this, so it fits the roundup better than a pitch.

items.title: A PTSD treatment with a '68% remission' rate: what that number does and doesn't mean
items.angle: A short, skeptical item on a headline remission rate: what the treatment is, how big and long the trial was, and what remission means in trial terms.
items.why_now: Trial results were publicized Oct. 22 and the 68% figure is the kind of number that travels.
items.is_it_real: So far this rests on a single ScienceDaily summary. The trial phase, sample size, comparator and journal are unconfirmed. It only runs if the writer can find the paper, and it should not be upgraded to a pitch on this evidence.
terms: PTSD treatment — 68% remission rate, clinical trial

items.title: KFF's fall poll: who Americans trust on vaccines now
